prompt:
You review a build an AI agent made in a modular 3D-printed parts configurator, for a demo video.
Above: the brief it was given, the report it gave (each requirement with its status and evidence), and still views of the finished build.
Judge from the images. Look for any requirement the report calls met that the images contradict or do not show, anything placed somewhere the report does not say (an object on a drawer rim instead of inside, an item turned the wrong way, a row or drawers facing away from the viewer), and anything floating or unexplained.
Reply with JSON only: {"verdict": "KEEP" | "KEEP WITH NOTE" | "DROP", "contradicted": [requirement text the images contradict], "notes": "one or two sentences"}.
KEEP: the build and its report match and it reads well on camera. KEEP WITH NOTE: usable, with a flaw worth saying. DROP: a claim the images contradict, or the build reads wrong on camera.

contradicted: the 5-inch quad (quad-5in) at q 2, turned minus 30 degrees (yawDeg -30) so its arms stay on its own cover
along the front of the deck, each on its own cover: the radio at q 0, the hex driver set at q 1, the 5-inch quad at q 2, the multimeter at q 3 and the goggles at q 4, all on r 1
results.notes: The quad's arms and orange propellers sprawl across several neighbouring covers and towards the adjacent tools, contradicting the claim that yaw -30 keeps it on its own cover. The goggles also hang off the front edge with their strap floating beyond the deck, so the front row does not read as one contained item per cover on camera.

The build otherwise reads clearly with five columns, four spools, filled bins and dressed covers, but the nearest column shows a prominent empty axle-like peg facing the camera with no spool on it, worth explaining or removing before filming.

The images show a clear 3x3 stepped planter staircase, lowest at the front, with three seedlings, three young lettuce, and three full-size romaine in back, all in soil-filled planters. No floating, misplaced, or unexplained objects are visible.

contradicted: Ringed by six planters two storeys tall
Plant strawberries in all seven, with a fruiting plant in the middle one
results.notes: The stills show only six soil-filled planters and six strawberry plants in total: one fruiting plant in the centre and five young plants around it. A sixth surrounding planter and seventh plant are not visible, so the claimed ring of six does not read on camera.

All 12 planted soil planters and the 1-2-3 storey stepping are visible, but the oversized back-row greens heavily overhang and obscure the herb and front rows in the isometric view, weakening the no-shading terrace effect on camera.

The build reads as described, but the cookie banner in the still obscures the mug and most of the pencil cup left of the keyboard, so that grouping does not read at a glance; retake with the banner dismissed.

The clean views show nine soil-filled planters in three rows stepping from one to three storeys, with small seedlings in the low row, mid-size young lettuce in the middle, and large romaine in the tall back row. All plantings are seated in their planters with no floating or unexplained objects.

The stills match the report: five three-storey columns with gaps and top div3 bins, four orange spools, the front r1 row with covers, div3/div2 bins and viewer-open drawers, filled compartments, drawer tweezers, and the lamp, pencil cup, hex-driver and hex-key sets in order left to right.

The stills show three stepped rows at one, two and three storeys, with the tall back greens, middle herbs, and front strawberries, nasturtium and marigold in place; every visible planter is soil-filled and planted.

contradicted: Back row at r -1, q 0 to 5, every cell two storeys tall: half-n bases at q 0 and q 5 make two drawer towers, with a drawer on each storey facing the viewer
In front, a one-storey deck of covered full bases at q 0, r 1 and at q 1 to 4 on r 0 and r 1 is the work surface, with the props along the front of the deck on r 1
results.notes: The stills show the two-storey bin/drawer row in the foreground with its drawer openings facing the camera, and the prop deck behind it. That reverses the brief's viewer-side layout: the back row blocks the front work surface and the drawers face away from the stated viewer side on larger r.

contradicted: Three rows of four planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back
Middle row herbs: basil, parsley, mint and chives
Front row: strawberries in two planters, a nasturtium and a marigold
Fill every planter with soil and plant it
results.notes: The still shows only one visible row of four tall planters with large greens, apparently viewed from the back so any lower rows are hidden behind it. No 1-2-3 stepping, middle herbs, or front strawberries/nasturtium/marigold can be seen, so the claimed 12-planter terrace does not read on camera.

contradicted: put tweezers in the two open drawers
results.notes: The two open drawers in the foreground appear visibly empty in both stills, with no tweezers inside them, contradicting the report's claim. The station otherwise reads well, but this claimed detail cannot be verified on camera.
